elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Section 10(a) as amended: "Kubient agrees to indemnify, defend, and hold harmless Customer, its affiliates, and its and their officers, directors, managers, members, agents, and employees" — express "defend" verb now extends to affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Same sentence covers "all third-party allegations, claims, actions, losses, expenses, damages, costs ... or liabilities (\"Claims\")" in favour of Customer and its affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: The trigger is all third-party Claims "arising out of or in connection with: (i) the Services; (ii) the Auction Platform" — an unqualified scope that necessarily captures third-party IP infringement allegations directed at the Services/Platform, with no IP carve-out retained.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Claims arising from "the Services" and from "(v) the acts or omissions of Kubient or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Kubient control with respect to Kubient's obligations hereunder" capture third-party claims founded on Kubient's unlawful acts in performing; item (iv) (breach of any representation or warranty) adds the compliance warranties. Coverage is by unqualified scope rather than a named 'breach of law' limb, which is acceptable but not expressly labelled.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: A third-party claim from unauthorised access caused by Kubient falls within "arising out of or in connection with ... the Services" and within limb (v) "the acts or omissions of Kubient or a third party hired by, employed, retained or under Kubient control"; no data-security carve-out is retained.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Limb (v) covers "the acts or omissions of Kubient" without any culpability qualifier, which is broader than and therefore includes gross negligence and wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Section 11(i): "the party seeking indemnification shall provide prompt written notice of the claim to the indemnifying party" (retained unchanged, with a favourable no-forfeiture-for-delay proviso).

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Section 11(ii): "the indemnifying party shall have the right to control the defense and all negotiations relative to the settlement", subject to consent for liability-admitting settlements.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Section 11(iii): "the indemnified party shall reasonably cooperate with the indemnifying party and its counsel at the indemnifying party's cost and expense."

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Section 10(b) as amended is cut back to "(i) the Content or Properties, including any allegation or claim that the Content or Properties violate or infringe on any third party rights, or (ii) Customer's breach of applicable Law"; the prior use-of-Services, breach-of-any-warranty and acts/omissions-of-Customer limbs are deleted.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Section 10(a) covers all third-party Claims arising out of the Services and Auction Platform, which encompasses IP infringement claims.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no such exclusion is required, and none is needed here because the retained indemnity is broader (no exclusions imposed on us).

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; absence of a combinations exclusion is more favourable to Customer and does not defeat the element.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specifications exclusion is present or required.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: Neither Section 10 nor Section 11 contains any procure/modify/replace remedy ladder; the redline does not add one (deliberately, since the preferred level is met).

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund-on-failure-of-remedies mechanic appears anywhere in the rendered Sections 10-11.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is stated; the Kubient indemnity is left uncapped in these sections, which is better for Customer.

reasons: Preferred checklist is complete: the two operations supply the only missing items (affiliates in the indemnified group at Section 10(a), and a narrowed Customer indemnity at Section 10(b)); the existing broad Kubient indemnity and the Section 11 notice/control/cooperation procedure already met the remaining eight elements.

Fallback is incomplete (no procure/modify/replace ladder, no refund fallback, no 3x super-cap), but that is immaterial because the preferred level is satisfied, and importing a super-cap would be worse than the current uncapped Kubient indemnity.

Minimality holds: only the indemnified-party list in 10(a) and the trigger limbs in 10(b) were touched. The deletions in 10(b) (unauthorised-use, breach-of-any-warranty, acts/omissions-of-Customer limbs) are exactly what the 'Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law' element requires; Sections 10(a)(i)-(v) and 11 are otherwise verbatim, including the favourable no-forfeiture-for-delay and settlement-consent provisos.
Intent is preserved: the mutual procedure in Section 11 still operates for both directions, no cross-reference is broken, and the Vendor-side allocation is unchanged.

Drafting nit to tidy (not a failure): Section 10(b)(ii) uses capitalised "applicable Law" — confirm "Law" is a defined term in the Agreement, otherwise use lower-case "applicable law" to avoid an undefined capitalised term.

Optional hardening (not required for completeness): the Vendor limbs cover IP infringement, breach of law, data breach and wilful misconduct only by breadth of "arising out of or in connection with the Services" and "acts or omissions of Kubient" rather than by name; if the counterparty later proposes narrowing limb (i)/(ii) or (v), insist on express IP-infringement, breach-of-law and unauthorised-access-to-Customer-Data limbs.
